Whereupon St. Augustine sticketh not to say, that good ministers do consider that "theym are but ministers; they would not be held for judges, they abhor that any trust should be put in them:" and that the power of remitting and retaining sins is committed unto the Church, to be dispensed therein, "notn according to the arbitrament of man, but according to the arbitrament of God." Whereas our adversaries lay the foundation of their Babel upon another ground: that "Christo hath appointed priests to be judges upon earth with such power, that none falling into sin after baptism may be reconciled without their sentence; and hath putp the authority of binding and loosing, of forgiving and retaining the sins of men, in their arbitrament."

Whether the ministers of the gospel may be accounted judges in some sort, we will not much contend: for we dislike neither that saying of St. Hierome, that, "havingq the keys of the kingdom of heaven, they judge after a sort before the day of judgment:" nor that other of St. Gregory, that the apostles, and such as succeed them in the government of the Church, "obtainr a principality of judgment from above; that they may in God's stead retain the sins of some and release the sins of others." All the question is, in what sort they do judge; and whether the validity of their judgment do depend upon the truth of the conversion of the penitent: wherein, if our Romanists
m Ministri enim sunt; pro judicibus haberi nolunt, spem in se poni exhorrescunt. Augustin. in evangel. Johann. tract. 5. op. tom. 3. par. 2. pag. 227.
n Non secundum arbitrium hominum, sed secundum arbitrium Dei. Id. de baptism. contra Donatist. lib. 3. cap. 18.
o Christus instituit sacerdotes judices super terram, cum ea potestate ut, sine ipsorum sententia, nemo post baptismum lapsus reconciliari possit. Bellarm. de poenit. lib. 3. cap. 2.

p Igitur in horum arbitrio munus solvendi et ligandi, et remittendi et retinendi peccata hominum, a Christo Domino, per Spiritum Sanctum fuisse positum, liquido constat. Baron. annal. tom. 1. ann. 34. sec. 197.
q Qui, claves regni coelorum habentes, quodammodo ante judicii diem judicant. Hieronym. epist. 5. ad Heliodorum. op. tom. 4. par 2. pag. 10.
r Principatum superni judicii sortiuntur; ut vice Dei quibusdam peccata retineant, quibusdam relaxent. Gregor. homil. 26. in evangel. op. tom. 1. pag. 1555.
